summary: The note surveys student-led environmental stewardship projects in a local school district launched after September 1, 2023. They include a green curriculum, a student symposium, a school garden, tech recycling, a clean commuting campaign, an eco storytelling club, and a district-wide alliance. Together they show students moving from learning about sustainability to taking action.
one_line: Student-led environmental projects across a school district since September 2023, from eco curricula and gardens to tech recycling and an inter-school alliance.
key_facts: Lincoln High School introduced the 'Cultivating Green Minds' program on October 15, 2023, developed by Elena Martinez and her team of educators to build environmental awareness into core subjects.

Under Cultivating Green Minds, biology classes focus on local ecosystems, history lessons cover environmental policies, and English classes study environmental literature from Rachel Carson's seminal work to contemporary journalism.
The Student Stewardship Symposium was held on November 12, 2023, organized by high school senior Michael Thompson, who argued that 'learning should be accompanied by doing.'
The Student Stewardship Symposium brought together students from various schools across the district to exchange ideas on environmental projects.
Jackson Middle School began 'From Seed to Sapling' on September 21, 2023, led by 13-year-old Sarah Cho and her science teacher Mr. Gregory, to turn underused schoolyard spaces into gardens.
The Jackson Middle School garden serves as an outdoor classroom for botany and ecology, with math students planning layouts and art classes decorating garden containers.
Franklin Tech High School sophomores, including Jason Lee, launched a tech recycling project on December 5, 2023, to collect and refurbish old electronics and recycle those that cannot be fixed.
The 'Clear the Air' initiative was launched January 20, 2024, by Mariana Flores and fellow students at Parkview Elementary to promote cleaner commuting.
Clear the Air organizes carpools, advocates for better cycling routes, and negotiates discounts with local transit for students.
The Eco Storytelling Club at Harper Magnet School was unveiled February 10, 2024, founded by English teacher Rebecca Green; students write stories, poems, and plays about the environment.
The Inter-School Environmental Alliance (ISEA) was formed March 15, 2024, with representatives from each school including Tomas Rivera and Aisha Khan.
ISEA acts as an umbrella organization to share resources, brainstorm solutions, and amplify individual initiatives; the note calls it the most ambitious project to date.
